title: The naive framing: "does Claude need to be trained?"
text: Someone wonders whether Claude needs special training to do earnings analysis. It doesn't need training at all. It needs briefing. One file tells it exactly what to do every time. A

title: A skill is a folder
text: Claude skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts. This one is called earnings analysis. It's skill. MD holds plain language instructions. No hidden code. Claude reads the file then acts on

title: Read, then execute
text: It. The instructions live in a step section. Claude reads each step in order then executes it. It's linear. No branching unless a step calls for it.

title: One job, stated plainly
text: This skill has one job. Turn a company's quarterly numbers into a written earnings update. 8 to 12 pages, a few summary tables, several charts. That's the whole brief. Anything outside it isn't part of what this file does. A Claude skill is a file, not training. It

title: Carry-out
text: Doesn't make Claude smarter. It gives Claude one job done the same way every time. Your turn. Paste this into Claude.

title: Your turn
text: I want a professional equity research earnings update. 8 to 12 pages, 3 to 5,000 words, covering beat or miss, updated estimates, and the revised thesis. Read the earnings analysis skill first and walk me through what you'll do before you do it. That clause matters. Asking Claude to explain the plan before running it surfaces the real constraints the file sets. Claude earnings analysis.

title: Outro
text: What one skill file actually does. Liam in for bear.
